dietEvidence.body: Herbivory is inferred from the broad snout and simple teeth. No gut contents are known, and the plants eaten are not preserved. The diet is a comparative inference for a titanosaur.

sizeNote: Length and mass are estimates from incomplete material, not measurements of a whole animal.
tagline: A relatively small titanosaur with bony armour plates embedded in the skin. It was among the first sauropods shown to have dermal armour.
summary: A relatively small titanosaur with bony armour plates embedded in the skin. It was among the first sauropods shown to have dermal armour.

discovery.body: Named by Bonaparte & Powell, 1980. The type series includes PVL 4017-92, a sacrum with fused ilia, from the Lecho Formation, Salta. Several partial skeletons and osteoderms are known.

fossilEvidence.title: Preserved material
fossilEvidence.body: Several partial skeletons, including armour and eggs.

fossilEvidence.title: Stratigraphic and geographic occurrence
fossilEvidence.body: Lecho Formation, Salta records the species in the Late Cretaceous. The numeric range used here is ≈76–70 Ma, an occurrence estimate rather than a direct date on every specimen.

anatomy.title: Preserved anatomy
anatomy.body: The body is covered in small osteoderms, the neck is moderately long, and the limbs are robust.

behaviour.body: The armour and eggs are preserved, but the armour arrangement is reconstructed and the eggs do not establish parental care. No trackway or social group is known. The relatively small body size and osteoderms are direct anatomy, not behavioural evidence.

reconstruction.body: A licensed life reconstruction is assigned to this record and credited in Sources and credits. The species is known from several partial skeletons, including armour and eggs. The reconstruction is an artist's interpretation of appearance, not a direct observation from the fossil record; preserved integument, where present, is described in the anatomy section, and the soft-tissue outline is otherwise inferred.

confidenceNote: Confidence is high for the osteoderms and presacral vertebrae. It is lower for the skull, armour arrangement, diet and behaviour. No complete skull or skeleton is known.
